explainBack.question: Why doesn't the $4 input / $20 output figure change what a Claude Pro subscriber pays each month?
explainBack.answer: Because those figures sit on a different meter. They are per-million-token usage charges for developers who pay Anthropic directly through the API — a software connection where you are billed by text processed. A subscription is a flat plan whose 'meter' is a usage limit within a time window (like the five-hour window), not a per-token bill. Anthropic changed the token prices on one meter and, separately, says it raised limits on the other; neither statement moves a subscriber's monthly price.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: A correct answer must distinguish per-token metered API billing (P004) from time-windowed plan usage limits (P003) and note the article's explicit statement that API figures do not describe monthly plan price (P006).
explainBack.assessment: The article supports this answer fully in ordinary language: P004 defines the API meter, P003 defines the subscription meter, and P006 states the non-overlap directly. Explain-back succeeds.

unseenTransfer.scenario: A freelance designer uses an AI writing tool built by a third-party startup that runs on Claude under the hood. After reading the Opus 5.5 announcement, she expects her tool's monthly fee to drop 20% and assumes she can now pick Opus 5.5 inside the tool.
unseenTransfer.question: Do the announced API price cut and the raised subscription limits change what she pays or which model she can use?
unseenTransfer.answer: Neither directly. The token price cut lowers what the startup pays Anthropic per million tokens processed — the startup may or may not pass savings on, since its subscription fee is its own pricing decision. The raised five-hour limits apply to named Anthropic subscription plans (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise), not to a third-party product. And 'available on all platforms' means developers can call the model; it doesn't mean her tool's interface exposes an Opus 5.5 option. She should check her tool vendor's own pricing page and model options, exactly as a Claude subscriber checks the model selector.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: Correct application of the two-meter split (P004: API charges are for those paying Anthropic directly), the plan-scoped limit statement (P002), and the availability-versus-selector boundary (P005).
unseenTransfer.assessment: The article's mechanism resolves this novel case cleanly — the intermediary layer follows directly from 'paying Anthropic directly' (P004) and the boundary logic of P005. Transfer succeeds.
